name: Background
summary: Surface backgrounds are white by default. A non-white background is allowed only for a sanctioned reason — a semantic feedback tint, the app-shell layout grey, an interactive state fill, or colour the human explicitly asked for — and always from an --aha-bg-* token. No gradients on any background or fill, except the AI affordance's border.
lead: White-first is the house default for every product-UI surface: cards, panels, page and section wrappers, modal and drawer bodies, table and list rows, tab panels. 'White by default' is not 'never any colour' — a handful of non-white backgrounds are functional and correct, and this pattern names them and the token each one binds to. What it rules out is decorative or brand colour on a surface with no functional reason to be non-white, any gradient fill, and raw colour literals. This pattern ships NO new component; the slide-type canvas / presenting stage is out of scope (it is theme-coloured by design — see the canvas guideline).

skillRef.note: The rule was born as the 'Backgrounds are white by default' section of the `background` guide; its binary judge is the DS anti-slop judge (`background` surface). The DS owns the enforceable criteria in anti-slop/criteria.json (surfaces.background, C1..C3). The plugin's colour names (--aha-colorSuccessBg, colorBgLayout, …) map to the live DS --aha-bg-* tokens used here.

surfaceChoice.example: --aha-bg-positive on a correct-answer panel, --aha-bg-negative on a failed-import banner

a hover / selected / active row, menu item or chip
the one sanctioned gradient — on the border only, the fill stays white
surfaceChoice.example: An AI prompt input with a gradient border and a white padding-box fill

componentBacklog: No missing components. The DS has no AI-gradient token yet: the AI affordance's border gradient is the one sanctioned gradient, but until a token lands it cannot be expressed token-only — add it here before a consumer needs it.

rules.rule: Leave neutral containers — cards, panels, page and section wrappers, modal and drawer bodies, table and list rows, tab panels — white or unset (--aha-bg-container). Paint a surface non-white only for a sanctioned reason: a semantic feedback tint, the app-shell layout grey, an interactive state fill, or colour the human explicitly asked for (say so in the PR).
Never tint a neutral container with brand or pastel colour 'for emphasis', and never use a feedback tint on a surface that isn't feedback — a green panel that isn't a success reads as one.
Use no linear-, radial- or conic-gradient as a background or fill. The only exception is the AI affordance: the gradient sits on the border (border-box) and the fill stays white (padding-box).

Bind every non-white background to a DS token — --aha-bg-layout, --aha-bg-hover, --aha-bg-positive / -negative / -warning / -informative — never a raw #hex, rgb() or hsl() literal, even when the literal is the right colour.

reuseNote: Doc-only pattern — the DS ships no background wrapper. The rule lives in the consuming app's styles; this pattern is the conventions + the binary criteria (anti-slop/criteria.json → surfaces.background) a consumer self-judges against.

selfCheck.label: every neutral container is white or unset; each non-white surface has a sanctioned reason
no gradient background or fill, except the AI affordance's border
every non-white background is an --aha-bg-* token, never a raw colour literal
